items.title: Make the loading state visibly readable at a glance
items.what: On the ShoeMoney loading screen, the progress bar in the lower third is only a very thin dark-brown line on a nearly black background, and the "Downloading the game" text above it is small and low-contrast. On a phone, the bar is easy to miss entirely.
items.why: This is the first thing players see. If they cannot instantly tell that loading is in progress, the game feels stalled or broken and early drop-off goes up.
items.how: Increase the bar height to roughly 8–10 px, brighten the fill within the same warm palette, add a clearly different track color, and show a percentage or file-progress value under the status line.

items.title: Remove the inactive sticks from countdown and rematch screens
items.what: On the "QUALIFIER / FIGHT IN 2–4" screens and the "HASANABI WINS / REMATCH IN 8" screen, the two giant joysticks still fill the entire lower half of the display even though the player cannot interact yet.
items.why: It creates noise, steals space from the matchup/result message, and implies the controls are live when they are not. On mobile, that is immediate confusion.
items.how: Fade the sticks, stick labels, and legend panel fully out during pre-fight and post-fight overlays, then animate them in only when the round becomes playable.

items.title: Make the core control legend legible instead of tiny
items.what: In the live fight screens, the bottom legend strip above the sticks packs 8 tiny labels and arrows ("step", "jump", "crouch", "reverse", "forward", "high", "low") into a short brown panel. Despite taking a lot of vertical space, the text itself is still very small at phone size.
items.why: This is a novel twin-stick control scheme; if the always-visible explanation is hard to read, onboarding suffers right when the player is trying to learn how to play.
items.how: Reduce each stick diameter slightly, increase the legend text size/weight, and simplify the wording into larger one-line cues or a first-round tutorial that can collapse after the player has seen it once.

items.title: Tighten the portrait camera so the fight reads larger
items.what: In the portrait gameplay shots, both fighters occupy a relatively small middle band of the screen. There is a large block of empty glowing dojo background above them and a large control block below, so punches and kicks read smaller than they should on a 390×844 phone.
items.why: This hurts the main game read: distance, contact, and timing are harder to parse when the actual combatants are not using enough of the available portrait height.
items.how: Push the camera in about 10–15%, reduce headroom above the fighters, and raise the tatami horizon so torsos and strike range dominate the center of the frame without clipping jump attacks.

items.title: Redesign the half-point display so scores parse instantly
items.what: On the HUD and the result screen, HasanAbi’s score appears as a small superscript-like "2½". The half is much smaller than the main digit, especially in the top-right scoreboard, so it reads like an annotation instead of part of the score.
items.why: Scoring is the player’s primary feedback. If a half point cannot be read immediately, the game feels unclear at the exact moment it should be most understandable.
items.how: Render half points with full visual weight—use "2.5", "2 + ½", or a dedicated half-point chip—and apply the same treatment consistently in the top HUD and the end-of-bout score card.
